findings.issue: Fallback for auth-service. When X-Internal-Client-Ip is absent, ClientIp returns request.getRemoteAddr(). auth-service runs with SERVER_FORWARD_HEADERS_STRATEGY=framework (deploy/aws/helm/ecommerce/values.yaml:140), so Spring's ForwardedHeaderFilter has already rewritten getRemoteAddr() to the leftmost X-Forwarded-For entry, which the client controls. For RequestDeviceContext (login throttle, device record) and AdminUserController audit, the fallback can therefore come from a forged XFF, which contradicts 'X-Forwarded-For is never read'. This is only reachable when the gateway removes the header (peer unresolvable) or on direct in-cluster calls, which are already inside the stated ClusterIP trust boundary. So it is not a new external bypass.
findings.fix: Have the gateway strip inbound X-Forwarded-For before proxying (or confirm SCG does not forward it). Alternatively, in auth use a ForwardedHeaderFilter limited to Host/Proto, or remove X-Forwarded-For before the framework filter. Add a test where auth gets XFF with no X-Internal-Client-Ip and the socket peer is used. At minimum, document this exception in ClientIp and ADR 0002.

summary: Slice-2 delta d195a937..b4abf171. All four consumers now read the client IP only through libs/common-web ClientIp. That covers AuditInterceptor, auth AdminUserController audit, auth RequestDeviceContext (login throttle and device record), the WalletController per-IP redeem key, and the user-service EngageController referral view and claim. ClientIp accepts exactly one header value that parses strictly (no DNS, 64-char cap, canonical form). It rejects multi-line and comma-joined values, never throws and never reads XFF. Spoofing from outside is prevented by the slice-1 gateway controls, which I re-checked. InboundHeaderSanitizationWebFilter strips the x-internal- prefix at order -300, and ClientIpPropagationGatewayFilter uses set or remove on proxied routes only. Services are ClusterIP, so a direct caller inside the cluster or VPC can still set the header, the same trust as X-User-*. The edge bypass remains B-4. Missing-header fallback is the socket peer. The wallet maps unknown to null, which skips the per-IP bucket while the per-user limit of 5 still applies. Auth and audit use 'unknown', as before. trustForwardedFor (and the prod override set to true) and user.referral.trustedProxyHops are removed, along with their Helm, env and docs entries. In main code, the only remaining XFF reader is the gateway's GatewayClientIp, plus auth's framework forward-headers strategy (minor 1). The referral IP check stays off by default, IPs stay HMAC-hashed, and no new IP logging was added. The audit IP field is now the real client IP, which is expected. The ClientAddress zone-id fix is correct: '1.1.1.1%x:80' is now rejected. The only dependency change is spring-kafka as testImplementation. There are no new endpoints, secrets or ledger changes. Helm values and deploy-aws.md name the B-4 release gate for all four consumers, so my slice-1 condition is met. Approve with three minor findings: auth fallback under the framework strategy, stale forward-headers docs, and the ADR gate wording.
